_comment: AUTEF v2 benchmark sample. Four projects spanning two orders of magnitude
in size, chosen so the sample varies on the three things that decide a
result: project SIZE, project LAYOUT, and how well the project is already
TESTED.
schema      988 lines   package   120 tests   -> tiny, generation-heavy
cachetools 1639 lines   src       333 tests   -> small, repair + mutation
sqlparse   4363 lines   package   507 tests   -> medium
boltons   17389 lines   package   519 tests   -> large
All four were measured with `autef2 check`: green with zero dependency
installation, in under 10 seconds each, pure Python with no C extensions.
Three of the four have no sys.platform branches at all, so their mutants
are killable on one operating system -- appdirs was rejected for the
opposite reason, 18 of 20 mutants being unkillable win32/darwin branches.
Every project is pinned to a commit. A manifest naming a moving branch
cannot be reproduced: tabulate went from 322 tests to 306 between two runs
of this benchmark, which is enough to change a coverage figure quoted in a
chapter. Re-pin deliberately, and say so when you do.
fault_kinds is declared deliberately. The baseline (v1) repairs a failing
test FUNCTION, so a file-scoped failure -- broken_import, broken_setup --
is one it cannot attempt at all. Seeding those measures reach, not repair
quality. This manifest therefore seeds only per-test faults, so both arms
can attempt every observation. Run manifest_reach.json separately to
measure the file-scoped case, and report the two apart.
Note on sample size: the exact McNemar test needs at least 6 discordant
pairs all favouring v2 before p < 0.05 is attainable. Four projects at 8
faults each is sized for that; one project never could be.
